subject: Residency exception criteria, sourcing checklist, and procurement timeline
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, procurement@healthcore.com
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Residency exception criteria + proposed evidence pack for Globex / HealthCore PoC

Hi all,

Quick background: Globex (Samantha) is asking for a narrow residency carveout for an APAC pilot that will process limited PHI-like telemetry (hashed IDs + usage signals). Legal has asked us to treat this as a conditional "residency exception" and demonstrate compensating safeguards in lieu of full onshore-only hosting.

Attached is a working Residency_Matrix_v2.xlsx that maps the request to our standard TIA/DTIA controls and the UK IDTA expectations. High-level asks from procurement:
- Clear list of what remains in EU/US vs what is routed to APAC edge nodes
- Kernel of technical mitigations (encryption-in-flight, short-lived KV cache TTLs, access controls)
- Evidence artifacts they can accept (SOC2 type II, KMS attestation, egress logs sampling)

Questions for engineering and security:
1) Can we commit to a prefix-only APAC cache (no long-term storage) and TTL <= 15m?
2) What telemetry or logs would we be able to provide as part of a TIA evidence bundle without exposing customer data?
3) If we do a staged rollout, what fallback routing would be acceptable to procurement (e.g., automatic failover to EU-hosted model if APAC capacity constrained)?

Proposed timeline (procurement asked for target): review this week, evidence bundle by Thurs 12/3, procurement checklist & DocuSign by 12/10.

I've included the two stub attachments (Residency_Matrix_v2.xlsx, UK_IDTA_Summary.pdf) in case procurement wants a single artifact.

Thanks — Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Senior Privacy Program Manager | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com

From: Samantha Ruiz <samantha.ruiz@globex.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, procurement@healthcore.com
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 14:18:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Residency exception criteria + proposed evidence pack for Globex / HealthCore PoC

Thanks Naomi — helpful starter. A few clarifications from our side:

- Scope: The pilot only sends hashed identifiers and short user signals (no free-text clinical notes). We still need the legal/ procurement — and our compliance team — to be able to show where the data lands and under what controls.
- Evidence: SOC2 report is fine; our procurement team usually wants an attestation that keys are customer-segregated (or that a KMS boundary exists). Will a KMS attestation PDF be sufficient?
- Fallback: Automatic reroute to EU-hosted endpoints is preferred, but we need a documented SLA (even if it’s a best-effort fallback) so our on-call teams know what to expect during failover.

Timeline: If Redwood can send the evidence bundle by 12/3 and a short statement of fallback behavior and cache TTLs, procurement can start the PO/DocuSign review. Can we also get an explicit statement on whether any subprocessors will be used for APAC edge routing? (Specifically: will storage/backups be touched by third parties?)

Samantha Ruiz

On Wed, Dec 2, 2026 at 2:18 PM Samantha Ruiz <samantha.ruiz@globex.com> wrote:
> Thanks Naomi — helpful starter. A few clarifications from our side:
>
> - Scope: The pilot only sends hashed identifiers and short user signals (no free-text clinical notes).

Thanks for the context. Quick technical answers to your asks:

1) APAC edge behavior: We can implement a prefix-only APAC KV cache and enforce a TTL of 15 minutes at the routing/proxy layer. No persistent long-term object storage will be written in APAC for this pilot.

2) KMS: Our standard flow uses a customer-dedicated KMS key option for Dedicated/Private customers. For hosted pilots we can provide a KMS attestation describing logical separation and rotation cadence; we cannot supply a dedicated customer KMS in hosted tier without a Dedicated commitment. If procurement needs a hardware-backed commitment (HSM), that triggers a Dedicated/private conversation.

3) Fallback & SLA: We can document a fallback policy — automatic routing to EU-hosted model when APAC pool is at 90% capacity or when latency exceeds threshold X ms. That will be a best-effort fallback for hosted pilots; we can provide operational playbooks and alerting hooks (push to their PagerDuty) but cannot guarantee hard SLAs without a Dedicated contract.

4) Subprocessors: APAC edge routing uses our CDN/edge partner for traffic routing only (no long-term storage). Backups and durable storage remain in EU/US regions managed by our cloud provider; we will provide a subprocessor list and the subprocessors that touch routing (edge/CDN) will be disclosed in the evidence pack.

I’ll prepare a short tech statement and a trimmed evidence list (SOC2 excerpt, KMS attestation, sampling of egress logs) for Naomi to fold into the procurement packet.

—David
